risk.title: Speed check
risk.none: The check found no shape known to run away. It is a set of rules, not a proof.
risk.nested_quantifier: A repeat inside a repeat. On text that almost matches, the time can double with every extra character.
risk.quantified_alternation: A repeated choice. If the choices can match the same text, the engine may try many combinations.
risk.adjacent_repeats: Two repeats in a row that can match the same characters. The engine may try every way to share them.
risk.leading_wildcard: The pattern starts with "any characters", so the engine retries from every position. Anchor it with ^ if it should start at the beginning.
risk.quantified_backreference: A repeated reference to a group. These can be slow on long text.
risk.large_repeat: A very large repeat count. The engine may reserve a lot of memory for it.
risk.blocked: Lists that filter on the page itself refuse a pattern marked high risk, because a slow pattern there cannot be stopped. Lists that filter in the background run it with a time limit.

warning.unicode_property: Python's built-in re has no Unicode properties (\p{...}). The third-party regex module does.
warning.set_operations: Set subtraction and intersection in a character class are specific to the JavaScript v flag.
warning.digit_unicode: In Python, \d, \w and \s also match non-ASCII digits, letters and spaces unless re.ASCII is set. In JavaScript they are ASCII only.
warning.dollar_newline: In Python and PCRE, $ also matches just before a final line break. In JavaScript it matches only at the very end.
warning.lookbehind_fixed: The look-behind can match text of different lengths. Python requires a fixed length, and PCRE requires each choice to have a fixed length.
warning.sticky: The sticky flag has no direct equivalent. Match from a set position in the calling code.
warning.indices: Group positions come from the match object in other languages, not from a flag.
warning.global_is_call: Finding all matches is a choice of function or option here, not a flag in the pattern.
warning.case_insensitive_unicode: Ignoring case follows slightly different rules for non-ASCII letters in each engine.

find.title: Search this page
find.body:
Type in Search this page in the page header to mark every place the text occurs on the page. The count shows which match you are on.
Press Enter for the next match and Shift Enter for the previous one. Escape clears the search.
The search ignores upper and lower case. To use a regular expression, write it between slashes, for example /kitchen|hall/i, or open the pattern builder from the button in the field.
A long list only draws the rows in view. To filter every row of a list, use the search field of the list.

patterns.title: Patterns in search fields
patterns.body:
Every search field takes plain text. Text between slashes is read as a regular expression, with optional flags after the closing slash.
The button at the end of a search field opens the pattern builder. It explains a pattern piece by piece, tests it against sample text, lists the matches and groups, and puts the finished pattern in the field.
Patterns are checked before they run. One that could take too long is refused, and the field says why.

appearance.title: Edit the appearance of anything
appearance.body:
Choose Edit appearance in the page header, then pick any element on the page. You can also right-click an element, or press Ctrl Shift E while it has focus.
The editor changes fill, text, shape, accent, size and opacity. Fills are layers: a colour, a gradient or a picture.
Apply a change to this one element or to every element of its kind. Undo steps back, Reset this removes the choices for the element, and Reset everything returns to the theme.
Choices are kept in this browser.

read_aloud.title: Read a page aloud
read_aloud.body:
Choose Read this page aloud in the page header to hear the text of the page in the language of the interface. Choose it again to stop.
Form fields, codes and passwords are never read.
Reading uses the voices of this device. If the device has none, the button is not shown.

history.title: History of your changes
history.body:
History lists the changes made in this browser to appearance, accessibility and open tabs, newest first, with the page each was made on.
Undo this change puts the choice back as it was before the change. Go back to this version puts it as it was right after.
A change to the private vocabulary is listed, but its text is not kept, so clearing the vocabulary leaves no copy behind. Locks are never listed.
History for automations is separate: Settings, Automations, History keeps every saved version in a repository.

export.title: Export a page
export.body:
Export makes a file from what the page shows now: its text and its tables, with the filter each list has at that moment.
Choose CSV for one table, JSON for tables and text as data, Markdown or HTML for a document, or plain text. You can download the file, copy it, or print it.
In CSV, a cell that starts with =, +, - or @ gets a leading quote so a spreadsheet does not run it as a formula.
The file is made in this browser. Nothing is sent anywhere.

locks.title: Lock a page
locks.body:
Choose Lock this page in the page header, or press Ctrl Shift L. A locked page can be read and searched, but nothing on it can be changed.
To unlock, hold the lock button for a moment. If you set a PIN, unlocking asks for it instead.
After three wrong PINs in a row the next try has to wait: 5 seconds, then 15 seconds, then 1 minute, then 5 minutes.
A lock is kept in this browser. It stops changes made by accident and casual use of a shared screen, and does not replace user accounts and permissions.

tabs.title: The bar of open pages
tabs.body:
Every page starts open as a tab, in the order of the menu. Close a tab with its close button; it stays closed until you open it again.
New tab lists every page and reopens closed ones. Open every tab reopens them all.
To close many at once, search in the New tab list, then close the tabs that match or the ones that do not. Undo brings them back.

menu.title: The tools of any element
menu.body:
Right-click any element, or press Shift F10 or the menu key while it has focus, to open its tools: edit its appearance, copy its text, read it aloud, or search everything.
The menu has its own search field. Escape closes it.

wording.title: Your private vocabulary
wording.body:
A private vocabulary file replaces words of the interface with your own. Drop the file anywhere on the window, or choose it under Profile, Localization.
The file is checked in full before it is used. A file that fails a check changes nothing.
The wording is kept in this browser until you clear it or load another file.

automation_history.title: Versions of automations
automation_history.body:
Every automation has its own repository, and every save is a commit. Settings, Automations, History lists every version.
Select versions to compare them, test them, run them, export them, or make one live again. Bulk test checks many versions at once without running any action.
Commit everything commits each automation that changed and then the master repository.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.body:
Ctrl Shift F searches everything.
Ctrl Shift E edits the appearance of the element that has focus.
Ctrl Shift L locks the page you are on.
Shift F10 or the menu key opens the tools of the element that has focus.
In Search this page, Enter goes to the next match, Shift Enter to the previous one, and Escape clears.
